chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding a man who made it upon himself to fast for a month, and he fasted fifteen days, then an issue arose for him, he was told: 'It is permissible for him to make up what remains of it, and if it is less than fifteen days, it is not permissible for him until he fasts a complete month.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever vowed to fast a specific day and broke his fast without an excuse, expiation becomes obligatory upon him as is obligatory upon one who breaks a day of Ramadan, and he must make it up.

38 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from al-Sayqal: that he wrote to him, 'O my master, a man vowed to fast a day for Allah, and marital relations occurred on that day; what is the expiation upon him?' He answered, 'He fasts one day in place of one day, and freeing a believing slave.'

39 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Mahziyar: that he wrote to him asking, 'O my master, a man vowed to fast a specific day and marital relations occurred on that day; what is the expiation upon him?' He (peace be upon him) wrote to him, 'He fasts one day in place of one day, and freeing a believing slave.'

40 - And it has also been narrated - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Bundar, the freedman of Idris, wrote, 'O my master, I vowed to fast every Saturday. If I do not fast it, what expiation is obligatory upon me?' He (peace be upon him) wrote, 'And I read it: Do not leave it except for an excuse, and fasting it is not obligatory upon you during travel or illness unless you intended that. And if you broke it without an excuse, then give charity for the count of each day to seven poor people. We ask Allah for success in what He loves and is pleased with.'

And this report, we have presented earlier, and there is no contradiction between this narration and the first two, because the expiation is obligatory according to the condition of the one breaking the fast. Whoever is able to free a slave, that is obligatory upon him; and whoever is not able to do that but is able to feed seven poor people, he gives that; and if he is not able to do that either, he makes up that day and there is nothing upon him. And this is as we explained regarding one who broke a day of Ramadan intentionally, not by mistake, and the ruling of the vow is as we explained.

41 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, who said: al-Husayn wrote to al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'I am your ransom, a man vowed to fast certain known days, he fasted some of them, then he fell ill and broke his fast. Does he start anew in his fasting or does he count what has passed?' He (peace be upon him) wrote, 'He counts what has passed.'

And as for what he mentioned (may Allah have mercy on him) regarding the ruling of the vow in the state of travel, we have explained it in what preceded in the Chapter of the Rulings of Travelers, and we have elaborated on it, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who vows to fast a month but breaks it due to illness or travel?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes these narrations to establish that a vowed fast (Nadhr) carries the weight of an obligatory fast, requiring a full month if less than fifteen days remain, and imposing the same expiation (Kaffarah) as breaking Ramadan for intentional interruption. The text highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of gradation in expiation, where freeing a slave is primary, followed by feeding six or ten poor people, and finally making up the day, reflecting the individual's capacity. This ruling underscores the binding nature of personal vows in Shia fiqh, treating them with the rigor of divine commands.
